summary:
Round 8, doc-only again. NO ASSERTION WAS WEAKENED: the only change under format/src/test is SubscriptionEventGrantTest's class javadoc and one .as() message; every predicate is byte-identical and .contains("byteStart=4096")/.contains("byteLen=65536") at :285-286 are untouched, as in rounds 6 and 7.

MY ROUND-7 FINDINGS ARE CLOSED AND I RE-CHECKED EACH. (1) The RTT predicate is now the symmetric form -- 'THE SECOND REQUEST, WHICHEVER IT IS, IS ISSUED BEFORE THE FIRST RESPONSE IS DELIVERED' -- and I could not break it: slice-then-header-sequential and header-then-slice-sequential are both false under it, a third speculative request reds the <=2 clause, and the only shape that greens it is the concurrent reader ADR-0044 prices at one saved RTT. (2) The tie-break landed as criterion 3b with the silent-failure reason (encodeRun CRC32Cs each run block) written down, and it now doubles as the assertion form the 'uses the event's coordinates' clause lacked: substituting reader.find(...).byteStart() reds 3b as well as the RTT clause. (3) The FetchPolicyConfig.DEFAULT_CROSS_AZ_MICRO_DOLLARS_PER_GB correction landed in both places with the cross-AZ-versus-GET distinction drawn.

THE ARITHMETIC IS TRANSCRIBED CORRECTLY AND I RE-DERIVED IT: DIRECTORY_ENTRY_BYTES = 49 (SegmentFormat.java:61), 1,600 * 49 = 78,400; saving = 2*objLen/(K+1) - 78,400 against one GET at 19,968 bytes gives 2*8,388,608/170 = 98,689 > 98,368 at K = 169 and 98,112 < 98,368 at K = 170, so 'positive to K ~ 169' is exact; bandwidth alone, 16,777,216/78,400 = 214.0 gives K <= 213. Both below ~400. One figure in the same paragraph is mis-attributed -- minor, detailed below.

BUT CRITERION 2 BREAKS A SEVENTH TIME, AND THE BREAK IS IN THE CLAUSE ADDED TO CLOSE THE ROUND-5 ONE. The boundary pair at K = crossover and K = crossover + 1 carries only a ONE-SIDED relation -- 'at most two requests' -- which is true of the whole-object path (1) as well as the bounded path (2), so nothing at the pair moves when the recorded crossover moves, and a threshold of K <= 1 leaves every case green with the measurement binding nothing. That is verbatim the defect criterion 1 says the pair exists to close. Second major: the request counts at every K > 1 -- 'ONE UNION SLICE' at the crossover and 'exactly the whole-object GET, one request' at ~400 -- both presuppose one fetch shared by a node's K ConsumerClients, which is M5.45h's criterion 1 by name, while this row depends only on M5.45g and says twice it may land first. Both repairs are one clause each.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'THE BOUNDED PATH IS AT MOST TWO REQUESTS AT EVERY K ... ASSERTED AT K = 1, AT K = crossover AND AT K = crossover + 1'), against criterion 1 ('THE CODE'S THRESHOLD IS DERIVED FROM THE RECORDED NUMBER ... two shares pin a threshold anywhere in [1, 400), so the cases are at K = crossover and K = crossover + 1, which is the only pair that moves when the recorded number moves')
findings.title: The boundary pair added to bind the measured crossover binds nothing: the relation asserted at both K = crossover and K = crossover + 1 is ONE-SIDED ('at most two requests'), which the whole-object path satisfies at 1 -- so a threshold of K <= 1 greens every case while the recorded number is unused
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION, and the cheapest one available: leave the recorded crossover at 169 in ADR-0044 and the derivedFrom-shaped computation in place, then branch on anything strictly below it -- `if (nodeRunCount <= 1) boundedRead() else wholeObjectGet()`, or an off-by-a-factor in the derivation (`threshold = crossover / 8`). Walk every clause of criterion 2 at the four shares it names. K = 1: the bounded path is taken, two requests, bytes = header + one 5.2 KiB run, strictly fewer than 8 MiB, the codec flag is read from the fetched directory and refused, 3b's disagreeing-extent fixture refuses, and the second request is issued before the first response is delivered. GREEN on every clause including the new RTT one. K = crossover (169): the whole-object path is taken, so ONE request is made -- and the assertion is 'AT MOST TWO REQUESTS', so 1 <= 2 passes. K = crossover + 1 (170): whole-object, 1 request, passes identically. K ~ 400: whole-object, one request, exactly the whole-object bytes, which is what the clause demands there anyway. Bytes are asserted at 'TWO SHARES ... not only at the two ends' -- the two ends being K = 1 and the ~400 share -- so no byte assertion exists at the pair to tell the two paths apart either. NOTHING REDS, and the bounded read this row exists to authorise is dead for every K >= 2 in production while the row is marked done. THE PAIR CANNOT SEE IT BECAUSE BOTH SIDES OF THE THRESHOLD SATISFY THE SAME INEQUALITY: 1 <= 2 and 2 <= 2. Criterion 1 names this exact outcome one clause earlier -- 'record a crossover of K = 40, branch at K <= 1, and both tested shares stay green while the measurement binds nothing' -- and the pair was the fix for it; the fix inherited the one-sided relation from the clause it was fixing, which is this task's half-landed-fix shape for the seventh time. derivedFrom does NOT backstop it: FetchPolicyConfig's derivedFrom is a code shape, not a behaviour, and a test that reads the constant back is a test of the constant, not of the branch -- the row itself says the number must be DERIVED 'NOT MERELY COMPARED TO IT'. THE REPAIR IS ONE CLAUSE AND COSTS NO EXTRA CASE, because the two cases already exist: state the relation at the pair as TWO-SIDED -- at K = crossover, EXACTLY TWO requests and strictly fewer bytes than the whole-object GET; at K = crossover + 1, EXACTLY ONE request and exactly the whole-object bytes. That pair is the only one that moves when the recorded crossover moves, which is what the criterion already says it wants and does not yet say.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 2, 'ONE UNION SLICE ... ASSERTED AT K = crossover', 'At ADR-0042's ~400-of-1,600 node share ... exactly the whole-object GET, one request', and 'the assertion is on the TOTAL' counted at M5.45g's byte source) against the same row's State cell ('depends on M5.45g') and body ('per-node residency is M5.45h's and this row has no dependency, so it may land first'), with M5.45h criterion 1 at backlog.md:69
findings.title: Every request count criterion 2 asserts above K = 1 presupposes one fetch shared by a node's K ConsumerClients -- which is M5.45h's criterion 1 verbatim -- so on this row's own stated ordering the counts can only be produced against a harness production does not use
findings.failure_scenario: ARITHMETIC ON THE PRODUCTION SHAPE. A node's K runs of one segment are K DISTINCT RunKeys -- SegmentWriter.java:32 keys runs by RunKey in a TreeMap, one run per key per segment -- and ConsumerClient.java:43-45 takes exactly ONE RunKey, with production building one per key in NodeSubscriptions.clientFor (plugin). So at K = crossover a node runs 169 ConsumerClients over the shared byte source. Criterion 2 requires the TOTAL through that seam to be at most two: one header range and ONE UNION SLICE across all 169 runs. A per-client cache in the seam cannot produce it -- each client wants a different slice, so the honest total is 1 + K = 170 -- and a union across 169 independently-arriving readNext calls needs a per-node HOLD or a barrier, which is M5.45h's criterion 1 ('a node holding K runs of one segment issues ONE fetch ... asserted at K = 64 ON ONE NODE through whatever holds that node's clients -- plugin is in scope') plus its criterion 2's residency bound, and M5.45h depends on M5.62. THE SAME IS TRUE OF THE WHOLE-OBJECT BASELINE, which is the half that makes this unarguable: 'at ADR-0042's ~400-of-1,600 node share ... exactly the whole-object GET, ONE request' counted as the total means 400 ConsumerClients share ONE whole-object fetch. Without M5.45h that is 400 whole-object GETs of 8 MiB -- the exact ~400-against-1 this row quotes M5.45h's cell to condemn. So criterion 2's baseline and its bounded arm both assume M5.45h has landed. SURVIVING DISCHARGE, and it is the cheap one: the owner lands after M5.45g and before M5.45h, cannot make 169 clients issue 2 requests, and takes the count by calling the widened seam ONCE with K ranges from a local driver -- the structural claim 'the seam is the ONLY path from ConsumerClient to bytes' is discharged separately by inspection, so nothing reds. The case then reports 2 at K = 169 while production reports 170, and reports 1 at K = 400 while production reports 400. That is verbatim the shape this row's own State cell warns about for the M5.45g dependency ('the owner discharges criterion 2 against a local harness production does not use') and verbatim M5.45h's own warning ('a unit case feeding 64 pairs to ONE fetcher passes while production issues ~400'). THE ROW HAS CONSIDERED M5.45h AND DECLINED THE DEPENDENCY ON THE WRONG GROUND: 'M5.45h's K = 64 case does not backstop it: this row has no dependency and may land first' answers whether M5.45h's ASSERTION covers M5.66, not whether M5.66's assertion needs M5.45h's MECHANISM. It does -- at every K > 1, on both arms. REPAIR, one of two, both one clause: either add M5.45h to the State cell's dependencies (and with it M5.62, which M5.45h depends on), or say explicitly that criterion 2's counts above K = 1 are taken through whatever node-level owner M5.45h builds and that this row therefore cannot land before it. The third option -- keeping the counts and the ordering -- is the one that leaves the harness discharge as the only satisfiable reading.

findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog.md:126 (M5.66 criterion 1, 'review measured that fixing the bounded path at two requests makes its extra cost one GET at every K, which on a request-only price wins up to K ~ 1,556'), against the same criterion three clauses earlier ('on dollars alone, in region, the bounded path NEVER wins -- it is +1 GET for $0 saved -- and a crossover of 0')
findings.title: The 1,556 figure is transcribed faithfully but attributed to the one price model that cannot produce it: I measured it on R12's byte-to-GET conversion with a TIGHT union, and under a request-only price the bounded path loses at every K, giving the crossover of 0 the same criterion states
findings.failure_scenario: THIS IS A CHECK OF MY OWN TRANSCRIBED ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH ONE LINE. The 169 and 213 figures are correct and I re-derived both against the tree (SegmentFormat.java:61, DIRECTORY_ENTRY_BYTES = 49; 1,600 * 49 = 78,400; 2*8,388,608/170 = 98,689 > 78,400 + 19,968 = 98,368 and 2*8,388,608/171 = 98,112 < 98,368, so K = 169 exactly; 16,777,216/78,400 = 214.0, so K <= 213). The 1,556 is also mine and also faithfully copied -- it is (8,192 - 78 - 19.5)/5.2 KiB = 1,556.6, my round-6 number, computed on R12's one-GET-equals-19.5-KiB-at-$0.02/GB conversion with the union assumed TIGHT (sum of byteLen). Its PRICE LABEL is wrong. Under a genuinely request-only price -- which is what cost.md and CostTable hold, and what the same criterion states three clauses earlier -- the bounded path costs 2 requests against 1 at every K and never wins, so the crossover is 0 and 1,556 is not derivable at all. The cell's other review-measured figure is labelled correctly ('On this row's own cited price -- R12, one GET against $0.02/GB -- ... a crossover near 331'), so the two are inconsistently attributed within one paragraph, and the owner is told in the same breath that the price model decides everything. WHY IT IS ONLY MINOR: the clause's conclusion is unaffected and is the one that matters -- 1,556 is far above ~400 under any reading, so 'the reason whole-object is right at ~400 is physical, not economic' stands, and the interleaved-fixture mandate that follows is the operative instruction. WHY IT IS WORTH A LINE: it is the figure this round was asked to check, and a reader who takes the label literally computes a crossover the label cannot yield. Recording it in the commit body is a sufficient answer under review.md rule 11; it should not open a fix round of its own.
